assumptions.condition: The equation matrix obeys \(W_{ii}=1\) for every \(i\in[q]\).
At most one coordinate of \(e\) has a Gaussian distribution.
Every structural error coordinate has nonzero variance: \(0<\operatorname{Var}(e_i)<\infty\) for every \(i\in[q]\).
Every entry of \(W\) is rational with total binary encoding length \(L\).
The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_X\).
The coordinates of \(\kappa\) are pairwise distinct.

definitions.name: Monomial ICA row orbit
definitions.construction: \([W]_{\mathrm{mon}}=\{\widetilde W\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}:\widetilde W=MW\text{ for an invertible monomial matrix }M\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized row-assignment candidate
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_q\) with \(d_{\pi,i}\neq0\) for all \(i\), set \(T_\pi=\operatorname{diag}(d_{\pi,1}^{-1},\ldots,d_{\pi,q}^{-1})P_\pi\), \(W_\pi=T_\pi W\), and \(B_\pi=I_q-W_\pi\).

definitions.name: Three-coordinate rational graph gadget
definitions.construction: Index coordinates by \((u_i,v_i,w_i)\) for \(i\in[n]\). Set \(B_G[\{u_i,v_i,w_i\},\{u_i,v_i,w_i\}]=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\ p&0&0\\ r&0&0\end{pmatrix}\), set \((B_G)_{u_i u_j}=g(A_G)_{ij}\), set all other cross-block entries to zero, and set \(W_G=I_{3n}-B_G\).

definitions.name: Independent switch assignments
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I(G)=\{S\subseteq V:(A_G)_{ij}=0\text{ for all }i,j\in S\}\), and \(\pi_S\) swaps \(u_i\) with \(v_i\) exactly for \(i\in S\) while fixing all other coordinates.

definitions.name: SCC-local equation matrices and counts
definitions.construction: Let \(\operatorname{SCC}(B)\) be the strongly connected components of the directed support graph with arrow \(j\to i\) when \(B_{ij}\neq0\); for \(C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)\), set \(W_C=W[C,C]\) and \(N_C=N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_C)\).

definitions.name: SCC-local stable enumerator
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Enum}(W)\) computes \(\operatorname{SCC}(B)\), enumerates each block's admissible perfect matchings by alternating-cycle recursion, normalizes each matching, certifies Schur stability by the exact rational Lyapunov equation, retains each stable local assignment once, and streams their Cartesian products in lexicographic component order.

definitions.name: Normalized monomial-row quotient
definitions.construction: The action is \((a,\pi)\cdot A=\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_q)P_\pi A\) for \(a_i\neq0\). Its normalized lift is \(\ell(A)\), its finite normalized orbit is \(\mathcal O_U(A)=\{\ell(MA):M\in\mathcal G_q\}\), and the quotient carries \(d_{\mathrm{orb}}(A,R)=\min_{M\in\mathcal G_q}\|\ell(A)-\ell(MR)\|_{\mathrm F}\). Compact normalized matrix sets carry the Frobenius Hausdorff metric \(d_{\mathrm H,F}\).

definitions.name: Normalized FOBI row lift
definitions.construction: From \(X^{(m)}\), compute \(\overline X_m=m^{-1}\sum_jX_j\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_m=m^{-1}\sum_j(X_j-\overline X_m)(X_j-\overline X_m)^{\mathsf T}\). On \(\{\widehat\Sigma_m\succ0\}\), set \(Z_{m,j}=\widehat\Sigma_m^{-1/2}(X_j-\overline X_m)\), \(\widehat F_m=m^{-1}\sum_j\|Z_{m,j}\|_2^2Z_{m,j}Z_{m,j}^{\mathsf T}\), \(\widehat A_m^{\mathrm F}=\widehat O_m^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_m^{-1/2}\), and \(\widehat U_m=\ell(\widehat A_m^{\mathrm F})\), where \(\widehat O_m\) is the measurably ordered orthonormal eigenbasis of \(\widehat F_m\). On the complement set \(\widehat U_m=I_q\).

definitions.name: FOBI covariance estimate and Gaussian critical value
definitions.construction: Let \(\widehat\psi_{m,j}\) be obtained from the Miettinen--Taskinen--Nordhausen--Oja joint FOBI influence function \(\psi_{\mathrm F}(X_j;P_X)\), after applying \(D\ell_W\) and vectorization, by replacing every population whitening matrix, FOBI eigensystem, and moment by its empirical analogue; set \(\widehat\psi_{m,j}=0\) if this plug-in expression is undefined. Set \(\overline\psi_m=m^{-1}\sum_j\widehat\psi_{m,j}\), \(\widehat V_m=m^{-1}\sum_j(\widehat\psi_{m,j}-\overline\psi_m)(\widehat\psi_{m,j}-\overline\psi_m)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(c_{m,1-\alpha}=\inf\{c:\Pr(\|Z_m^*\|_2\leq c\mid X^{(m)})\geq1-\alpha\}\) for \(Z_m^*\mid X^{(m)}\sim N(0,\widehat V_m)\).

definitions.name: Matrix-valued monomial-symmetrized FOBI confidence set
definitions.construction: Define the labelled matrix set \(\mathcal E_m=\{R\in\mathcal U_q:\sqrt m\,\|\operatorname{vec}(R-\widehat U_m)\|_2\leq c_{m,1-\alpha}\}\) and its quotient-invariant lift \(K_m=\{\ell(MR):R\in\mathcal E_m,\ M\in\mathcal G_q\}\). Equivalently, \(K_m\) is the union of the \(2^q q!\) signed-row-permutation images of \(\mathcal E_m\); arbitrary nonzero row scales are removed by \(\ell\).

definitions.name: Exact-pencil analytic homotopy handle
definitions.construction: For each intended switch set, eliminate the two leaf coordinates to obtain the exact characteristic pencil; isolate both critical-root disks by resolvent contours; invert the scalar critical-root coordinate analytically; and use a boundary-invertible matrix homotopy from the induced adjacency block to the Schur-complement correction while tracking zeros with multiplicity.

statements.statement: Can the exact-pencil analytic homotopy handle establish, uniformly over every simple \(n\)-vertex graph and every switch set \(S\), that the Schur complement has no poles on the chosen contours, that zero multiplicities are preserved through the inverse coordinate, and that a negative eigenmode of \(A_G[S,S]\) persists if and only if \(S\notin\mathcal I(G)\)?
statements.justification: This is the graph-uniform multiplicity-and-no-pole step on which the complete orbit realization depends.
statements.gap: The presolve derivation supplies explicit contours and perturbation bounds, but no independent proof has yet certified the matrix-valued homotopy for every graph.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution validates the coefficient gadget used by Theorems 1 and 2; a counterexample kills this realization before complexity claims are made.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_q\), including the nondegeneracy condition \(0<\operatorname{Var}(e_i)<\infty\) for every \(i\in[q]\), square ICA identifies \([W]_{\mathrm{mon}}\) from \(P_X\). If \(\widetilde W=MW\) for an invertible monomial matrix \(M\), re-referencing induces a bijection between the admissible normalized assignments of \(W\) and \(\widetilde W\) that preserves their normalized coefficient matrices. Consequently \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(\widetilde W)=N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\), so the stable count is a population-law functional rather than a labeling-dependent count.
statements.justification: The proposition closes the identification step that turns a matrix-representative count into a causal functional of the observational law.
statements.gap: The ICA literature states sign, scale, and permutation indeterminacy, but stable-orbit counting requires an explicit normalization-preserving bijection across representatives.
statements.consumer: Any population or sample procedure may start from an arbitrary ICA labeling without changing the reported stable count.

statements.statement: For every simple \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\), let \(e\) have independent, centered, variance-one, continuous non-Gaussian coordinates and set \(X=W_G^{-1}e\). Then \((P_X,W_G,e)\in\mathcal M_{3n}\). For every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_G)\), the transformed errors \(T_\pi e\) remain independent, centered, continuous, and non-Gaussian with positive coordinate variances, so every normalized assignment is a legal same-law cyclic LiNG mechanism.
statements.justification: The counting reduction must live inside the causal model rather than only inside rational matrix algebra.
statements.gap: The matching representation permits row rescaling, but the reduction still must verify that its chosen error family is closed under every normalization in the complete orbit.
statements.consumer: The proposition licenses interpreting each counted assignment as a distribution-equivalent cyclic LiNG mechanism.

statements.statement: For every simple graph \(G\) on \(n\geq1\) vertices, the rational construction with \(\varepsilon_n=[2^{40}(n+1)^4]^{-1}\), \(g=\varepsilon_n^2\), \(\delta=\varepsilon_n^3\), \(p=-25/16\), and \(r=(15/16)(1-\delta)\) satisfies \(\rho(B_G)<1\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_G)=\{\pi_S:S\in\mathcal I(G)\}\). Every independent intended assignment obeys \(\rho(B_{\pi_S})\leq\max\{9/10,1-\delta/10\}\); every non-independent intended assignment has an eigenvalue of modulus at least \(1+g/20\); every other admissible assignment is unstable; and \(W_G\) has \(O(\log(n+1))\) bits per nonzero entry.
statements.justification: The theorem turns a global spectral filter on a causal equivalence class into an exact, coefficient-valid combinatorial family with explicit margins.
statements.gap: Lacerda et al. screen assignments and prove a disjoint-cycle uniqueness result; they do not realize arbitrary independent-set systems or control every unintended row permutation.
statements.consumer: It supplies the missing stability-conditioned orbit oracle boundary for matching-frequency calculations in cyclic-LiNG intervention design.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal R_q\), computing \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions. Unless \(\mathrm{RP}=\mathrm{NP}\), no FPRAS exists even on matrices \(W_G\) obtained from graphs of maximum degree six. In contrast, \(N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W)=\operatorname{per}(\mathbf 1\{W\neq0\})\) has an FPRAS. Membership in \(\#\mathrm P\) is witnessed by a permutation and verified exactly by rational normalization followed by the Lyapunov certificate \(H-B_\pi^{\mathsf T}HB_\pi=I_q\) with \(H\succ0\).
statements.justification: The result separates an approximable matching orbit from the causally relevant stability-filtered suborbit on the same normalized-assignment representation.
statements.gap: Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda cover the unfiltered permanent, while Sly covers independent sets; the missing theorem is the one-call rational causal realization linking them.
statements.consumer: It tells the matching-frequency sampler of Sharifian et al. that its permanent guarantee cannot be inherited after imposing equilibrium stability.

statements.statement: For every \(W\in\mathcal R_q\), admissibility and stability factor over the original support SCCs: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\cong\prod_{C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_C)\) and \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)=\prod_{C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}N_C\). The bijection is restriction and concatenation in a fixed topological SCC order.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact modular unit of stable causal ambiguity rather than merely an invariant graph partition.
statements.gap: Sharifian et al. prove SCC invariance, and Lacerda et al. use block triangularity for disjoint cycles, but neither proves a Cartesian product of normalized stable assignment fibers.
statements.consumer: Small feedback modules can be counted and audited independently before their stable alternatives are combined for intervention planning.

statements.statement: The algorithm \(\mathsf{Enum}(W)\) emits every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) exactly once. If \(c=|C|\) and \(e_C\) is the number of admissibility edges in block \(C\), its local screening time is \(\sum_C O((c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C))\operatorname{poly}(c,L))\), after which Cartesian-product output has \(O(q)\) delay per stable assignment. The claim is output-sensitive in the enumerated local matching fibers and does not assert polynomial delay in \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) alone.
statements.justification: The bound makes the positive algorithmic content exact without hiding rejected local matchings behind a polynomial-delay claim.
statements.gap: Uno enumerates unfiltered perfect matchings, while prior local causal discovery does not integrate normalized Schur screening or SCC products.
statements.consumer: The procedure is an exact fallback for stable matching frequencies when the largest feedback SCC is small.

statements.statement: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_q^{\mathrm{FOBI}}\), whose structural errors satisfy \(0<\operatorname{Var}(e_i)<\infty\) for every \(i\in[q]\), the plug-in covariance estimator obeys \(\widehat V_m\to_{\Pr}V_{\mathrm{FOBI}}\), and the matrix-valued symmetrized set satisfies \(\liminf_{m\to\infty}\Pr\{N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\in C_m^N\}\geq1-\alpha\). Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm H,F}(K_m,\mathcal O_U(W))=O_{\Pr}(m^{-1/2})\) in the normalized-row Frobenius topology, equivalently the underlying estimator contracts in the quotient metric \(d_{\mathrm{orb}}\). Both assertions are pointwise in the fixed law; no uniform graph-support, shrinking-kurtosis-gap, zero-normalization-boundary, or unit-circle-boundary guarantee is made.
statements.justification: Region-first inversion respects ICA indeterminacy and avoids differentiating an integer-valued functional.
statements.gap: Miettinen et al. stop at a labelled FOBI matrix limit, while generic set-inversion work does not handle the monomial ICA orbit and Schur-normalization discontinuities.
statements.consumer: Applied cyclic-LiNG analyses can report count uncertainty without claiming uniform support recovery or selecting an arbitrary ICA labeling.

sampling_model.design: Population identification uses a square fully observed cyclic LiNG model with nondegenerate error coordinates; inference uses an independent observational sample and an explicit matrix-valued FOBI region on the row-scale and permutation quotient.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent draws from one fixed \(q\)-variate equilibrium law.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no treatment variable in the core identification theorem; a later atomic intervention reveals a matching edge and is the downstream consumer.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The sample covariance whitens the data, the eigensystem of the sample FOBI matrix estimates row directions, \(\widehat V_m\) is the empirical covariance of plug-in normalized-row influence functions, and \(c_{m,1-\alpha}\) is the conditional Gaussian norm quantile. No graph support is assumed known, and all coverage and contraction claims are pointwise.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: LiNG-D outputs the complete distribution-entailment equivalence class and stability selects at most one candidate when the true graph has disjoint cycles.
Distribution-equivalent cyclic LiNG graphs correspond to perfect matchings, their SCCs are invariant, and unfiltered matching samples estimate intervention reward.
The permanent of every nonnegative matrix has a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme.
Counting independent sets is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete even for graphs of maximum degree three.
Unless \(\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}\), no FPRAS counts independent sets on graphs of maximum degree six.
All perfect matchings of a bipartite graph can be enumerated in output-sensitive total time with linear work per matching after preprocessing.
Under bounded eighth moments and distinct kurtoses, the FOBI unmixing estimator has an explicit joint root-sample-size expansion.
Inversion of a sample criterion yields confidence regions for an identified parameter set with consistency and coverage theory.
Discontinuity of a functional prevents nontrivial locally uniform confidence procedures in general.
StableSpIn learns cyclic linear models under the absolute spectral-radius restriction \(\rho(|B|)<1\).

tldr: A fully observed cyclic LiNG law identifies a finite monomial row-assignment orbit, but equilibrium stability imposes a global spectral filter on that orbit. The core theorem constructs, from every simple graph \(G\), an explicit rational \(3n\)-variable equation matrix \(W_G\) whose complete stable assignment set is exactly the independent sets of \(G\). This yields \(\#\mathrm P\)-completeness and bounded-degree approximation hardness for the stable count even though the unfiltered assignment count is a permanent with an FPRAS. Exact SCC factorization supplies a local algorithmic fallback, and an explicit matrix-valued symmetrized FOBI region gives pointwise orbit-honest count coverage while contracting to the normalized orbit. The unresolved content is the graph-uniform analytic determinant homotopy that must preserve multiplicities and exclude poles for every intended switch set.

project_justification.gap: Published cyclic-LiNG methods enumerate or sample the full normalized row-assignment fiber and use stability only as a candidate-level screen. They do not classify the complexity of the filtered count or justify transferring permanent-based sampling guarantees after the spectral restriction.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a coefficient-valid realization theorem that controls normalization, signed feedback cancellation, every unintended permutation, and a polynomial-bit spectral margin simultaneously.
project_justification.fill: The proposed rational graph gadget identifies stable assignments with independent sets, transfers exact and approximate counting lower bounds, factors the count over SCCs, and attaches pointwise uncertainty quantification that respects the full ICA orbit.

related_work: Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer characterize the complete LiNG-D row-permutation fiber and show that Schur stability can narrow it, but their uniqueness result is confined to disjoint cycles and their discussion leaves efficient stable search open. Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash represent the same ambiguity by perfect matchings, prove SCC invariance, and estimate intervention rewards from unfiltered matching samples; these results provide the setup and the direct consumer rather than a stable-count theorem. Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda provide the FPRAS benchmark for the unfiltered permanent. Greenhill and Sly provide the exact and bounded-degree approximation-hardness donors for independent sets. Uno supplies the alternating-cycle enumeration primitive adapted only after SCC factorization is established. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja supply the FOBI linearization, while Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer motivate region-first inversion and Pfanzagl explains why the final guarantee must remain pointwise at discontinuity boundaries. Misiakos and Püschel study the stronger absolute contractivity constraint \(\rho(|B|)<1\), not counting over normalized ICA assignments.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite exact checks reproduce the complete orbit equality for \(K_2\), \(P_5\), \(C_5\), \(K_{1,4}\), and \(K_5\), with stable counts \(3,13,11,17,6\), but these checks do not prove the universal contour argument. The early kill test is to audit the exact pencil, the inverse-coordinate equations, the \(4gn^2\) perturbation bound, the negative-mode rectangle homotopy, multiplicity preservation, and absence of poles. A sign error, hidden pole, unintended stable permutation, or loss of polynomial-bit margins kills the construction. The enumeration result is output-sensitive in local admissible matchings, not solely in stable outputs.
honest_scope: The graph gadget and its determinant homotopy are open and constitute the theorem-level kernel. Conditional on that realization, the counting reductions are standard but must still be written with exact promise and approximation conventions. SCC factorization, pointwise confidence-image coverage, and normalized-orbit contraction are supporting results. Region contraction does not yield singleton count consistency at a discontinuity, and no almost-uniform sampler for the stable orbit, uniform graph-support recovery, or stability-conditioned adaptive-submodularity theorem is claimed. In the acyclic special case every SCC is a singleton and the factorization reduces to the unique LiNGAM row order; when \(G\) is edgeless, Theorem 1 reduces to all \(2^n\) intended local switches being stable, matching \(|\mathcal I(G)|=2^n\).

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Section 5.3, Theorems 3--6, their proof constructions, and Section 6 were read. The paper defines stability by \(\rho(B)<1\), proves uniqueness only for disjoint cycles, exhibits cancellation and multiple stable candidates for touching cycles, and explicitly asks whether stable models can be found without traversing all candidates.
seed_details.question: Does the complete Schur-stable normalized row-assignment orbit of an explicit rational cyclic LiNG mechanism realize the independent-set family of every simple graph, with uniform radial margins and no unintended stable assignments?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's cycle-product argument, which ceases to characterize stability for touching cycles, by an exact leaf-elimination pencil and an analytic inverse coordinate near the critical conjugate roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Schur-stable perfect-matching counting, stable LiNG-D counting complexity, and ICA row-permutation stable-orbit counting returned the LiNG-D and 2025 matching papers but no theorem on the target pair.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from LiNG-D because that algorithm already enumerates admissible permutations and tests eigenvalues. Rebuttal: enumeration gives no coefficient-valid realization theorem, no counting reduction, no graph-uniform margin, and no exclusion of all unintended permutations.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Sections 4.1--4.2, Theorem 4.4 and its two-direction proof, Section 7, and the Conclusion were read. The paper proves SCC invariance and represents the observational class by perfect matchings, but neither theorem factors the stability-filtered assignment set.
seed_details.question: When does the stable normalized assignment orbit equal a Cartesian product of SCC-local stable orbits, and what exact-once output-sensitive local enumeration bound follows?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Strengthen SCC invariance to a statement that every admissible permutation cycle remains inside an original SCC and that normalization preserves block triangularity for every assignment.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found local cyclic LiNG recovery and unfiltered perfect-matching enumeration, but no stability-filtered SCC product theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: block-triangular eigenvalues make this immediate. Rebuttal: the missing issue is prior to spectral testing, namely proving that matching feasibility and normalization do not couple SCCs; once that congruence is established the spectral step is short.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Section 5.2, Theorem 8 and its linearization, and the Discussion were read. The theorem gives the joint first-order expansion of FOBI under bounded eighth moments and distinct kurtoses; the paper leaves the sign-permutation indeterminacy in the ICA functional and does not project uncertainty through a discontinuous causal-orbit count.
seed_details.question: Can an explicit matrix-valued FOBI region on the row-scale and permutation quotient be inverted through \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}\) to obtain pointwise orbit-honest coverage while the region contracts to the normalized orbit?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the published FOBI chart but symmetrize the entire matrix region before applying the discrete normalization-and-stability image map, rather than selecting one labeling and differentiating the count.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent searches found criterion-region inversion for set-valued parameters and impossibility at discontinuous functionals, but no confidence image for a stability-filtered ICA orbit count.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: coverage is a tautological projection of any confidence region. Rebuttal: the supporting result must specify the normalized matrix lift, quotient action, plug-in covariance, calibrated critical value, and pointwise orbit contraction before the discrete confidence image is well defined.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 6.8 and its induction proof, Section 7's matching-frequency estimator, and the Conclusion were read. Adaptive submodularity is proved under the uniform law on the full matching orbit, and the estimator samples that same unfiltered law.
seed_details.question: Characterize whether adaptive diminishing returns survives conditioning the matching prior on Schur stability, or give a minimal failure family and a replacement regret guarantee.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Recompute conditional marginal gains under the stability-filtered posterior; the published induction that deletes realizations can fail because spectral conditioning correlates edge outcomes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches on stability-conditioned matching frequencies and cyclic LiNG intervention design found no conditioned-law theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: conditioning a prior cannot affect pointwise submodularity. Rebuttal: adaptive submodularity is a distribution-dependent inequality in conditional expected gains, so correlated edge indicators can reverse it.
seed_details.drop_reason: The exact conditioned-law frontier would require a second major policy theorem and sampler beyond the stable-count kernel; it remains a concrete consumer rather than a coequal proposal claim.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 5.3 and Section 6 were read. The paper's signed feedback example shows that cancellation can make \(\rho(B)<1\) even when a positive cycle is individually expansive, while its disjoint-cycle theorem isolates the cancellation-free case.
seed_details.question: Give an SCC- and sign-pattern-level necessary-and-sufficient condition under which \(\rho(B_{\pi})<1\) and \(\rho(|B_{\pi}|)<1\) agree for every admissible assignment, and quantify the maximal orbit-count separation otherwise.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace signed cycle products by a diagonal-sign similarity or balanced-signed-digraph certificate that is preserved under row normalization, then prove necessity by a generic cancellation family.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination paper StableSpIn was opened at its abstract and method summary; it optimizes under \(\rho(|B|)<1\) but does not compare the two predicates across an ICA assignment orbit.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Perron--Frobenius already gives \(\rho(B)\leq\rho(|B|)\). Rebuttal: that one-sided inequality neither characterizes orbit-wise equality nor controls how many Schur-stable assignments absolute contractivity discards.
seed_details.drop_reason: No credible route to a necessary-and-sufficient orbit-wide characterization emerged without a substantially separate signed-matrix theory.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The carried prior-proposal receipt states that its square reduction projects postintervention-solvable row assignments onto an effect frontier and explicitly excludes stability-refined completions; this verified gap, rather than any unpublished theorem claim, is the anchor.
seed_details.question: Characterize the sharp equilibrium-effect set obtained after filtering every normalized square LiNG assignment by Schur stability, with a stable same-law witness for every retained effect value.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the prior rank-only completion certificate by simultaneous nonzero-normalization, invertibility, and spectral-feasibility certificates before projecting onto the response ratio.
seed_details.destination_search: The adjacent published cyclic-LiNG effect and finite-structure confidence-set threads do not supply a stability-filtered sharp projection.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the answer is merely to enumerate candidates and discard unstable ones. Rebuttal: a publishable result needs an evaluable sharp formula and exact witness theorem, neither of which follows from brute-force filtering.
seed_details.drop_reason: The current evidence supports a finite algorithm but not the demanded analytic sharp frontier or singleton criterion.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Abstract, Introduction, Main Theorems 1 and 2, the gadget construction, proof-technique discussion, and open-problem discussion were read. The method encodes hard-core phases in random bipartite gadgets; at \(\lambda=1\) it gives no FPRAS for maximum-degree-six independent-set counting unless \(\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}\).
seed_details.question: Can a rational cyclic LiNG family realize the full hard-core partition function \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal I(G)}\lambda^{|S|}\) as a weighted stable-orbit functional and inherit the uniqueness-threshold approximation transition?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Augment each intended local switch with a multiplicity or rational weight while preserving the all-permutation spectral exclusion; the unweighted coefficient gadget does not provide such a weight map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weighted Schur-stable ICA assignment partition functions found no target-method paper.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: assign weight \(\lambda\) to every switch and the result is immediate. Rebuttal: the causal orbit count is unweighted and normalized row assignments do not carry arbitrary Gibbs weights, so a law- or multiplicity-valid encoding is a new construction.
seed_details.drop_reason: The required causal interpretation of assignment weights is absent, so the seed risks becoming a formal partition-function analogue rather than an identified causal object.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 4's constrained-rooks construction, Section 5.3's stability screening, and Section 6's explicit search question were read. The paper supplies no structural parameter under which the spectral filter can be incorporated into dynamic programming.
seed_details.question: Is exact stable-orbit counting fixed-parameter tractable in the treewidth of the admissibility graph together with SCC size, using a finite spectral certificate state?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace matching-only separator states by a compositional representation of the characteristic or Lyapunov certificate under partial row assignments.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found bounded-delay unfiltered perfect-matching enumeration but no treewidth algorithm for a global Schur predicate over normalized assignments.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Courcelle-type machinery makes any bounded-treewidth counting problem routine. Rebuttal: Schur stability of rational coefficients is not a finite-label local predicate, so finite-state compositionality is precisely the unresolved step.
seed_details.drop_reason: No finite separator summary for exact spectral stability was found.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The publisher abstract, Theorem 1.1 summary, construction overview, and final approximation statement were opened. The paper anneals over perfect and near-perfect matchings to obtain an FPRAS for every nonnegative permanent, but its state weights depend only on matching structure and matrix entries, not on a global spectral predicate after row normalization.
seed_details.question: Derive a checkable margin or density frontier under which rejection or annealing from the unfiltered matching orbit yields an FPRAS for \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}\), and prove failure beyond that frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is the conductance comparison: a Schur-stability filter can delete an exponentially dominant portion of the matching state space and need not preserve paths through near-perfect matchings.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Schur-filtered perfect-matching annealing and stable-assignment FPRASs found no occupied pair.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: if the stable mass is inverse-polynomial, rejection sampling is immediate. Rebuttal: that is only a sufficient promise; the novel object would have to derive a structural threshold from observable matrix primitives and show its converse.
seed_details.drop_reason: The substrate supplies no non-tautological matrix-primitive frontier, so the candidate fails the M2 derived-frontier gate.

literature_map.opened_locations: Introduction; Sections 4, 5.2, 5.3, and 6; Theorems 1--6 and their displayed proof constructions.
literature_map.settled: The population LiNG-D output is the complete admissible normalized row-permutation class. Schur stability can select a unique member for disjoint cycles, while touching cycles can leave several stable members.
literature_map.unsettled: The paper asks for a way to search stable models without visiting every admissible candidate and gives no stable-orbit counting classification.

literature_map.opened_locations: Introduction; Sections 4.1, 4.2, 6, and 7; Theorems 4.4, 6.8, their appendix proofs, and the Conclusion.
literature_map.settled: Admissible cyclic-LiNG graphs correspond to bipartite perfect matchings, SCCs are invariant, an atomic intervention reveals a matching edge, and the unfiltered eliminated-graph reward is adaptive submodular.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither matching sampling nor adaptive gains are conditioned on equilibrium stability.

literature_map.opened_locations: Jerrum--Sinclair--Vigoda Theorem 1.1 and approximation construction summary; Sly's Abstract, Introduction, Main Theorems 1--2, gadget construction, proof-technique discussion, and open problems.
literature_map.settled: Every nonnegative permanent has an FPRAS, whereas independent-set counting at activity one has no FPRAS on maximum-degree-six graphs unless \(\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{RP}\).
literature_map.unsettled: No coefficient-valid reduction transfers that separation to the Schur-filtered normalized ICA orbit.

literature_map.opened_locations: Dai et al. abstract, problem statement, and identifiability summary; Uno's theorem and complexity summary for perfect-matching enumeration.
literature_map.settled: Local cyclic-LiNG alternatives can be recovered from a Markov blanket, and all bipartite perfect matchings can be enumerated in output-sensitive total time.
literature_map.unsettled: Neither result gives exact SCC factorization of the stability-filtered orbit or output sensitivity after the spectral test.

literature_map.opened_locations: Miettinen et al. Introduction, Section 5.2, Theorem 8, its proof linearization, and Discussion; Chernozhukov et al. criterion-inversion theorem summary; Pfanzagl abstract and discontinuity result summary.
literature_map.settled: FOBI has a joint root-sample-size expansion under bounded eighth moments and distinct kurtoses; region-first inversion can protect nonsmooth images; nontrivial locally uniform confidence can fail at discontinuities.
literature_map.unsettled: No result symmetrizes a FOBI region over the monomial orbit and inverts it for the integer-valued stable count.

literature_map.opened_locations: Publisher page, abstract, objective summary, and stated spectral-radius regularizer.
literature_map.settled: StableSpIn enforces \(\rho(|B|)<1\) in a sparse-input likelihood program.
literature_map.unsettled: The paper does not characterize agreement with signed Schur stability over normalized ICA row assignments.
